answer.value: Based on the data analysis, alcohol consumption appears to have a minimal impact on most health indicators. However, there are some notable trends: Heavy drinkers show slightly higher vitamin A intake (0.393 vs 0.385 for non-drinkers), while non-drinkers have slightly higher vitamin D levels (0.250 vs 0.240 for heavy drinkers). The most significant finding is that vitamin D levels are universally low across all groups (average 0.243), suggesting a potential widespread deficiency regardless of alcohol consumption. Symptoms count is also relatively low across all groups, indicating that most individuals in the dataset do not exhibit severe deficiency symptoms.

key_insights: Heavy drinkers have slightly higher vitamin A intake (0.393 vs 0.385)
Non-drinkers have slightly higher vitamin D levels (0.250 vs 0.240)
Vitamin D levels are universally low across all groups (average 0.243)
Symptoms count is relatively low across all alcohol consumption levels
